name: Brake pads
summary: Replaceable friction blocks that press against the disc. They are meant to wear out instead of the disc.
whatItDoes: Pads provide the friction that slows the car. They are the brake part you will replace most often.
howItWorks: Each pad is a steel backing plate with a block of friction material bonded to it. The caliper pushes one pad against each face of the disc. Many pads have a small metal tab or an electrical sensor that warns you when the friction material is getting thin.
failureSymptoms: High-pitched squeal from the wear indicator
Grinding (metal on metal: stop driving and inspect)
Brake pad warning light (on cars with wear sensors)
safetyNotes: Brake dust is harmful to breathe. Don't blow it off with compressed air; use brake cleaner and a cloth.
Replace pads in axle sets: both sides together.
Pump the brake pedal until it feels firm before driving, to bring the pads back against the discs.
